closingLine: Each figure is from a peer-reviewed paper or official source. None of them are controversial in isolation. The synthesis is what is missing.

cards.headline: UAE Quaternary aquifer fresh groundwater storage, 1969 → 2015
cards.context: Fresh groundwater storage in the UAE Quaternary aquifer is reported to have fallen from roughly 238 km³ in 1969 to about 10 km³ by 2015 — a decline of approximately 96% over four and a half decades of abstraction outpacing recharge.

cards.headline: Artificial recharge vs. natural recharge
cards.context: Across Gulf arid aquifer systems, engineered recharge (injection, infiltration, return flows) is estimated to run at roughly five times the natural recharge rate — meaning the subsurface increasingly reflects what we put in, not what nature delivers.

cards.headline: Al Ain has been flooding from rising water tables
cards.context: Rising shallow groundwater in Al Ain has produced surface flooding and infrastructure damage documented in the literature for around fifteen years — an early, visible symptom of water accumulating in the wrong compartment.

cards.headline: Subsea pipeline to discharge TSE the land cannot absorb
cards.context: A reported 4 km subsea pipeline is intended to discharge treated sewage effluent the landscape can no longer absorb — an explicit acknowledgement that reuse capacity on land has limits.

cards.headline: DECCA's age — the authority that should own the integrated question
cards.context: The Dubai Environment, Climate Change Authority (DECCA) was established under Dubai Law 11/2024 and is roughly eighteen months old — a young authority still building the framework within which the integrated subsurface question could sit.

cards.headline: Salinity excess of the Gulf vs. typical seawater
cards.context: The Arabian Gulf is reported to sit around 25% saltier than typical open-ocean seawater, reflecting high evaporation, restricted exchange, and concentrated brine discharge — the receiving body for the region's desalination chain.
